linkedin.text:
🚨 Your AI coding agent just sent you three paragraphs when you needed one command.

You asked how to fix your auth flow. It replied with Great question, gave you context about middleware, rambled about dependency versions, then buried the actual fix somewhere in the middle.

You scrolled. You re-read. You finally found the answer.

12,485 developers got tired of that workflow and installed i-have-adhd — a plugin that rewires Claude and Codex to lead with the action, number the steps, and cut the recap.

✅ Every response starts with the command you need to run
✅ Multi-step tasks get numbered lists, not prose
✅ No preamble, no Hope this helps, no tangents

The plugin enforces 10 rules: action-first structure, visible wins, matter-of-fact errors, and capped lists. You install it once with one CLI command and your agent stops burying answers in backstory.

Search i-have-adhd on GitHub and check the before/after table in the README. What coding agent response pattern drives you the most crazy?
